significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that the measurable shift called “own-belief contamination” predicts later “own-voice factual leakage,” a form-(iii) predictive coupling, while steering the “belief-ownership” direction would add a form-(ii) causal claim about insulating that behavior. This would establish both a phenomenon—false-persona role-play produces persistent factual errors—and a mechanism—partially entangled ownership representations mediate those errors—thereby fixing expectations about which role-play episodes should later fail, rather than merely showing that beliefs are decodable. The negative branch is also informative and determinate: contamination near zero with no excess leakage over matched false-content controls would support clean persona/own-belief separation, although failure of steering alone would rule out only this proposed intervention; this bears directly on how self/other belief representations in “Language Models Represent Beliefs of Self and Others” and the distinctions questioned by “Language models cannot reliably distinguish belief from knowledge and fact” should be interpreted. After topic substitution, generic research on LLM beliefs would not retain the specific contamination-to-future-error coupling or ownership mechanism, so the topic alone would not earn this score.

reach.justification: The claim hands downstream users two named handles: the “contamination score,” which is proposed to predict errors, and a “belief-ownership direction” that can be steered to insulate the model while preserving role-play. The score is ex ante because it is measured during persona adoption and predicts “factual errors after role-play,” leaving an action window for screening or steering before the later own-voice answer; the proposed consumers include practitioners using customer-support, educational-debate, and jailbreak-persona systems, not only belief researchers. Although the steering vector would need re-extraction per model, the broader asserted relation survives recalibration: “the degree of own-belief contamination is measurable and predicts factual errors,” so a newly calibrated model is expected to show the same directional coupling across factual domains and persona types rather than merely offering a procedure with no predicted result. Under topic substitution, LLM-belief research alone supplies neither this forward predictor nor the insulation knob, so the reach score comes from claim-specific handles and lead time rather than the topic’s general importance.
